human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in marshes and other wet areas with low, dense vegetation, and may also be found in other areas with dense shrubs; less commonly found in dry areas. It uses shrubby, wet ground rather than tended gardens, and is uncommon in dry country, so it is placed on damp, densely vegetated ground.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Nests in low vegetation, laying 3-5 eggs in a cup-shaped nest, with both parents feeding the young. Males generally arrive at the breeding site before the females, males arriving on average about five days earlier, because they set up territories first.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Regional note, a judgement informed by the sourced range and migration pattern rather than a cited statement about this state: the nominate G. t. trichas covers southeast Canada and the east USA, and 'In the northern parts of its range the birds are migratory, wintering in the southern parts of the breeding range', so West Virginia is treated as a summer breeding ground that is largely vacated for the winter, with a small resident share.

vocalizations.description: A loud, emphatic twichety twichety twichety twich, repeated from a low perch in dense vegetation.

taxonomy.note: GBIF backbone gives family Parulidae and authority (Linnaeus, 1766); ITIS scientific-name search returns TSN 178944 with the same authority. Linnaeus originally described it as Turdus trichas; the current combination is Cabanis, 1847.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2489670 from species/match; ITIS TSN 178944 from the ITIS scientific-name search; NCBI taxon id 135433, eBird code comyel and IUCN category least concern (Q211005) from Wikidata P685, P3444 and P141.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005). The Conservation status section records a decline in numbers 'due to loss of favored habitat' but notes the species 'is still very common'.

range.note: 'ranging from southern Canada to central Mexico. In the northern parts of its range the birds are migratory, wintering in the southern parts of the breeding range, Central America and the West Indies.' The Central American and West Indian country list is the described wintering region rather than a per-country breakdown, so it is recorded at country level and should be read as approximate.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop is an authored reading of a small warbler moving through low dense vegetation, and Fly is powered. The source describes insects 'usually captured in dense vegetation, but sometimes caught in midair' without naming gaits, so only these two modes are claimed rather than adding Walk or Glide.

traits.nest_type.note: 'Common yellowthroats nest in low vegetation, laying 3-5 eggs in a cup-shaped nest.'

traits.perching.note: Perches in dense vegetation to sing and forage; the male sets up and holds a territory before the females arrive.

traits.senses.note: hearing High from the loud repeated song used by males to hold territories; vision_color authored from the black facial mask, which females are described as preferring in larger males, implying a colour cue. No olfaction value is written because no sourced claim was found.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (0.00954 kg falls in the Tiny band, under 0.05 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 9.54 g and AVONET Mass 9.54 g agree exactly (both sourced to Dunning 2008) and sit inside Wikipedia's 7.6-15.5 g range, which is wide because it spans thirteen subspecies.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the Measurements range 11-13 cm.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the Measurements range 15-19 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement, and an honest gap: no openly licensed source consulted states a mean or typical longevity for this species, and none was found. 2.5 years is an authored order-of-magnitude figure for typical adult longevity of a small, largely migratory warbler, where first-year mortality dominates. Treat it as a placeholder, not a measurement.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 100, agreeing with 'These birds feed on insects, which are usually captured in dense vegetation, but sometimes caught in midair.'

traits.social.note: Authored from the territorial behaviour described in the Migration section, where males arriving first 'set up territories before the females arrive' and females 'appear to prefer males with larger masks', which is a territorial pairing system rather than a flocking one. The source names no flocking behaviour outside migration, when birds move in loose nocturnal migrants.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal = 0. Note that the source calls the northern populations 'nocturnal migrants', which is a migration habit rather than an activity pattern, and the foraging, nesting and song are all daytime.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the source describes no predator-directed behaviour at all, only territorial song and the black mask used in mate choice, so Flee is recorded as a default for a small marsh warbler and this is an honest gap.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: an abundant breeder that lives in dense cover and is described as 'very common', but a bird that keeps to low, dense vegetation is harder to approach than an open-country feeder, so a middling value is used.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-understory 80 + ForStrat-midhigh 20 (100) mapped to arboreal, consistent with 'usually captured in dense vegetation'. The ground share of 0.2 is authored judgement, reflecting the low, marsh-edge nesting and the genus name's 'ground-' root (Geothlypis combines Greek geō- 'ground' with thlupis).

habitat.shelter_tag.note: 'Common yellowthroats breed in marshes and other wet areas with low, dense vegetation' and 'They may also be found in other areas with dense shrubs'; nesting and roosting are both in that cover.

habitat.resources.note: Food weight 1.0 on invertebrate follows traits.diet. Nesting weight 1.0 on nest_cup follows the nest description. shrub_thicket carries the highest shelter weight because the source names dense low vegetation and dense shrubs as the habitat the species is actually in; perch at 0.5 is authored judgement, since no open source quantifies the relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Authored: the source places the bird in marshes, wet areas and dense shrub, and explicitly says it is 'less commonly found in dry areas', so Adapter is used with uses_gardens set to false rather than claiming garden use the source does not support.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'In the northern parts of its range the birds are migratory, wintering in the southern parts of the breeding range, Central America and the West Indies. Southern forms are largely resident.'

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement: the source contrasts migratory northern birds with 'largely resident' southern forms without giving proportions, so 0.2 is an authored figure for the share of the species' population that overwinters on its breeding grounds.

seasonal.phases.note: The breeding window is an authored narrowing: the source gives a clutch size and both parents feeding the young, and separately gives spring migration from early February to late May, so the May-July window is a judgement placed after the male-arrival and breeding part of that migration period. The US-WV regional phase is likewise a judgement from the nominate subspecies range plus the stated migration pattern, and is labelled as such in its own note. No open source dates this species' breeding season in West Virginia.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Authored: the source gives a 3-5 egg clutch and says both parents feed the young, but gives no incubation, nestling or independence timings, so the 60-day juvenile duration and the 0.7 scale are both judgements, and the egg stage carries no duration because none is sourced.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The song is a loud twichety twichety twichety twich', from the Description section.

vocalizations.call.note: 'Its call is a soft jip', from the Description section.

vocalizations.note: Descriptions from the Description section; months, time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the Description section (olive backs, wings and tails, yellow throats and chests, white bellies, and in adult males a black face mask 'stretching from the sides of the neck across the eyes and forehead, which are bordered above with white or gray'). The breast is coloured from the accent slot for the yellow bib and an extra face_mask part renders the male's black mask; females and first-year males have a faint or absent mask, so the model shows the adult male. Proportions are authored judgement for a small, round, short-beaked warbler.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag keeps the program's invertebrate default, which is this species' only food. flee_m kept short (4 m) for a small bird that stays in dense cover. song and alarm point at the described song and contact call respectively; the program expects an alarm call and the source's 'soft jip' is the only non-song call described, so it is used for both the contact and alarm roles. nest_m1/nest_m2 are the authored May-July nesting window.
